utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T. The Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric Simic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. The Trial Chamber has observed that there is a confidential motion by the Prosecution regarding the testimony of Witness O. In order to discuss it, we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution. Any other witnesses or any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Let me -- I will just perhaps first address the matter for the witnesses and then my colleague may address you on other matters. We do not have any more witnesses. There was another witness who we were to call. I don't want to mention his name because this is one of his concerns. We are not calling him because, as I said, he is in a situation where he's at property back in Bosanski Samac. He's been subject to intimidation and feels that he would not have security if he were to testify and that protective measures would not guarantee people in the municipality not finding out and that could increase for him the difficulties he's experiencing. So in terms of witnesses, Witness O was our final witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Obviously, we're very close to the point now where the Prosecution is in a position to close its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't want to proceed quite to that point yet, if I may. There are some other matters that I may -- I think we can attend to in the meantime, namely, the production of various documents and so on, which I hope we can do now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That will take some time as we produce them to the Court and they're given various exhibit numbers. I would, however, like to formally close, if it's convenient with the Chamber, tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I wanted to remind the Prosecution, the last time before we closed for the summer recess, talking about -- discussing Dr. Gow's evidence. I remember you mentioned something like tabling it formally and having the documents numbered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Translations of Dr. Gow's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because all those are part of the Prosecution evidence, so you can't formally close before they are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly right. I can attend to some of those matters now and deal with that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But when I've done that, I don't want to be - if it's okay with the Chamber - pressed to finally close, and I prefer to do that, if I may, tomorrow. There's -- I've already had an opportunity of discussing the general position of the case with my colleagues, but there's some other matters that I want to raise with them. It won't, in effect, cause any great delays. We've obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Di Fazio. You can proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- well in advance of our expected closure date by the end of the week. Thank you. If Your Honours please, can I produce the English translations of P61, P -- sorry. Would you just bear with me for one moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We've got the English translations of the various documents that we discussed on the last occasion the Chamber sat, and perhaps if we deal with them one at a time. Perhaps P61 first. That should now enable that particular exhibit to be given a full exhibit number. Thank you. P62. The next one was P63. And the remaining document is P67. I do apologise. The second-to-last exhibit is P67.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise to Mr. Di Fazio. I was given a document which I understand is P62, 03066247, ERN number. They were given to me one at a time. I just need to know whether they're part of the same document or whether they are ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have clarification, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Copies are being given to registry, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we get more documents, we'd like to make sure that our numbering is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what is the correction?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe if I could just have one clarification from our colleagues. We have just received one document with the ERN number 48121. Is that P67 or P64?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The number which Defence counsel has just read out, that is ERN 48121, that is P67. The document which the registrar read out earlier, which was 03066247, is P63, and it's entitled Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with a number BH 317942.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is now corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful to my colleagues. Now it's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the registry and my colleagues from the Prosecution to see whether the document P67 has an ID mark on it. I think that this document was introduced during the testimony of Mr. Vitozovic and I think at the time it was an ID document, the one that is now P67.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It had to be translated, and he also produced the original of the document, and it's that that's being produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it wasn't waiting for translation; it was a full exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Awaiting translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's check with the registry assistant, I think, because the records should be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe I could be of assistance. I've read the transcript on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what happened was that the witness himself produced this document, the original, out of his jacket, so to speak. He didn't have with him, of course, an English translation, because it was his document, so it was given an ID number, and a Prosecution number, although it was introduced during the cross, but it was given an ID number because at that time we only had the B/C/S version and no English version. That's what comes apparent if one reads the transcript from day it was tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have confirmation? I see Mr. Lukic shaking his head. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we have two problems here. However, I don't have the document on me. But I think that this is where the problem is: This document is the one that Mr. Fitozovic said was his, talking about how he swam over the river, crossed the river, and there was another document that I produced, and that was also given an ID mark. The problem is that that document had already been introduced as P14, or P19, and it was my document, and it was tendered in by the Prosecution. This is why I would like for us to wait before deciding on this document until tomorrow, when I will bring what I have with me and we can clarify this issue. But I think it would be ridiculous to have this document tendered in through the Prosecution during Mr. Lukac's testimony, and then when I tried to introduce that document, then the Prosecution objected to that. And this is why I wanted to wait until tomorrow, until I can produce that document here in court so that we can clarify it and avoid these problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Lukic. We can wait for you to search for the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think the matter has been clarified by the registry. The document which you -- the Defence produced was numbered D53/3 ID, and the reason it was given an identification number only was because the witness said that it was a forgery, and then it was agreed that you, during the Defence case, would call evidence to clarify the status of the document. D53/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It's D50/3. D50/3, not 53. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That document was introduced as an ID document. And during our summer recess I was able to determine that that very document that I tendered here in the courtroom was -- had been introduced by the Prosecution during Lukac's testimony, and it was tendered in at that time. This is all I wanted to clarify, so that there are no misunderstandings here. When Mr. Fitozovic started mentioning that document, then the Prosecution was allowed to once again tender in the document that had already been introduced six months prior to that. I had that document, and Mr. Fitozovic also had the document on him, and I think that this is where potentially a problem can arise. I cannot verify this now because I don't have the document with me at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll leave this until tomorrow, when you can look at the documents that you have, and also the Prosecution can revisit this matter, so that we get the correct numbers and we also know which one is the Prosecution Exhibit and which one will remain a Defence Exhibit. Any other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, if Your Honours please. The testimony of Dr. Gow, you recall, that was one of the last matters that we discussed, and as Your Honour raised this afternoon. The testimony is available now. We've printed off copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It comes from two cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Those are transcripts?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Transcripts, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In the other trials.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Together with the exhibits that were referred to by the witness in that testimony. So from the two cases. It's just a question of handing it up and getting exhibit numbers. Now, can I ask you this: Do you want the transcript and the exhibits attached to that transcript all given the one Prosecution Exhibit number, or do you want separate numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think we can have one single number and then have maybe A, B, C, D, or /1, /2, so that they're kept together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's what I was going to suggest, with respect. Thank you. Two separate exhibit numbers, one for the Tadic testimony and one for the Celebici testimony of Dr. Gow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you can take us through one, one transcript, and then whatever exhibits are attached, so we clearly number them, and then we go to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. May I just confer with my case manager?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps if we deal first with the Tadic testimony of Dr. Gow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Whichever one is ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. We have copies to provide. If the Tadic transcript, if Your Honours please, goes from page -- from numbers 9367 to 9055. Once the transcript has been given a number, I can give you the first of the exhibits that is attached to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we move on to this Tadic transcript, may I take it that P61, P62, and P67 are admitted into evidence? I'm sorry. I apologise. P61, 62, and 63. P67 will remain for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I take it there is no objection from the Defence. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They are admitted into evidence and they will retain the same numbers as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Exhibit for the Tadic hearing will be P144. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, therefore, can the first exhibit be given its subnumber? It will be -- the exhibit is "My View of the Break-up - Army Without a State" by Veljko Kadijevic, and we have that -- bundles of that particular exhibit available now. So I take it that will become P144A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let the registry assistant deal with that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This exhibit will be P144A. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the next attachment to the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is P144A. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. The next attachment to the transcript is the International Conference on the former Yugoslavia Arbitration Commission, opinion number 11, also known as the Badinter Commission. Could that be given exhibit number P144B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that is confirmed. It's 144B.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. If Your Honours please, may I produce the next attachment to that transcript of Dr. Gow. It's resolution number 752 of 1992 of the United Nations Security Council adopted at its 3075th meeting on the 15th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P144C, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That completes the attachments for that particular exhibit, if Your Honours please. May I move now on to the Celebici transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I produce the transcript of the evidence of Dr. Gow from the Celebici case, ask that it be given an exhibit number, and then I'll proceed to provide the attachments, or exhibits that arise from that evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Celebici transcript will be P145, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May I produce the first attachment? For the sake of brevity, perhaps we can call it Variant A and B document. It bears the same title as that document, instructions for the organisation and activity of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P145A, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The next subexhibit, if Your Honours please, is excerpts from the diary of Borislav Jovic, entitled "The last days of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," and dated the 5th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P145B, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That completes that task. Can I just ask that we go back to the issue of translations? I omitted to hand up one remaining translation, and that is Exhibit P134. It's demographic results. It arose during the testimony of Ewa Tabeau. It was a document produced to her by Mr. Pantelic. The translation of that document has been produced and I now provide the translation. It can be given its full exhibit number, 134 ter, P134.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. P134 ter and P134 are now fully admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: While on Dr. Tabeau, there was the supplementary report which she handed in. I doubt if it was given an exhibit number. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right. The supplementary report was filed, not not given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, was it was filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DE FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I am sorry. I haven't attended to that yet. I can get copies of that and provide that to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We got copies at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You have copies? I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because it was filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. I would seek --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We just want the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- seek that it be given a formal identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If we can go back to the first one and use the same number and then perhaps call it "A." Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are on the same topic, I would kindly ask my learned friend to provide us with additional copies of B/C/S language translation of the Ewa Tabeau supplement, for the benefit of our client, I mean the annex that you submitted. It's not a question of time. I mean, we are not in a hurry, but just for the record, maybe we could get --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I'll make sure that that's attended to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. All right. Can we have the number for it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The expert report of Ms. Ewa Tabeau is P133. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, perhaps we could name that the addendum --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- report, expert report, of Dr. Ewa Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can I have the registry assistant's attention?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. I would just appreciate the Office of the Prosecution to provide the registrar with a copy, because I don't have a copy of that addendum. It needs to be obviously also provided to the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I was under the impression that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can do that, provide you with copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we just have the formal title again, Mr. Di Fazio? You said that it should be called the addendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think we can entitle it "Addendum to the expert report of Dr. Ewa Tabeau."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And the original -- Ms. Reidy correctly points out, I think, that the original report was P133. This addendum report -- now, I'm not quite sure how you would like to -- what numbering you would like to give it. Would you like it to be called P133A or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it makes better sense if we have it as part of P133.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then we have it as P133A.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. That would be -- that would make sense. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That doesn't end the issue of documentation. There is an issue that the Prosecution is currently speaking to the Defence about, and that concerns exchange records. We'll be in a position to finally deal with that tomorrow if you now grant my application for an early adjournment to enable us to attend to these last-minute matters. As I said earlier, we'll be able to proceed then smoothly to the final closure of the Prosecution case, I expect, tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall adjourn our proceedings and continue tomorrow at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Sorry. I saw you rather late.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm not trying to get the last word. I just would like to respond to briefly what my colleague said earlier, at the beginning of the session, about my departure from the Tribunal and the kind words from the Bench. I'm not often lost for words, but I was taken a bit by surprise, so I just wanted to thank my co-counsel and the Bench for their kind words, but just also to place on the record that it has been an extraordinary privilege to have had the opportunity to work for the Tribunal and, in particular, to appear before this Chamber and to be part of the work of this Tribunal. It's something -- an area of law which I personally have a very strong commitment to. So I appreciate also what has been for the main part a very friendly and cooperative relationship that we've had with Defence counsel, and I think we all do get on very well and have good friendly as well as professional relations. So thank you to counsel and to people from the registry and the senior legal officers, who have been very, very cooperative and helpful, when necessary, to me in my role as one of the lawyers from the OTP. So I wish you continued success in continuing this case. I didn't expect it would have gone on this long. I thought I might have seen the end of the case. But that's not how it worked out. So I wish you the best, and again, thank you for your kind words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also if you allow me, Your Honour, on behalf of my colleagues and also our clients, we wish all the best to our learned friend Ms. Reidy in her future professional career and life, and although sometimes we were hotly in dispute and disagree, but that's part of our profession. Nothing personal. We all work our job. And maybe this is a good opportunity, a professional and personal suggestion to Ms. Reidy prior to her leave from this institution. Ms. Reidy, please drop the charges against our client and be happy in your next life. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic. Thank you. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 1415. We wish you well, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of September, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.23 p.m.,
